summary: Final map addition before the run's budget expires (action=research, map_path=maps/core-v1.json, base version 12). It records the Raft.Restore reporting ambiguity as a sourced deferred surface rather than only in a feedback record: the entry point 'Raft.Restore error reporting after a completed restore' notes that Raft.Restore returns the confirmation no-op's error, so a leadership loss or enqueue timeout that prevents the no-op from committing is reported the same way as a restore that failed before replacing the FSM, while the applied state and burned index have already changed, and the docs say only that the call blocks 'until the restore is complete or an error occurs'. The open questions - whether the two cases should be distinguished and whether callers rely on the current single error when deciding to re-issue - are kept explicit, and the surface cites S-api-restore-doc, S-api-restore-noop and S-raft-restoresnapshot. As an addition it needs no map_changes entries and changes no existing object. Run state at submission: six confirmed_in_scope conclusions across eight implementation_reproduced findings, every previously recorded map surface mapped, and the residual frontier limited to that deferred reporting surface, the FSM batch manager details, the tcp transport stream/pooling code, and the TimeoutNow-without-term residual.
